stemBlocks.value: OACB is a parallelogram in which OA = a and OB = b. (a) Express the vector OC in terms of a and b. (b) Express the vector AC in terms of a and b.
Think first: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and parallel, so they represent the very same vector.

contentBlocks.value: In parallelogram OACB, AC is opposite and parallel to OB, so AC represents the same vector as OB

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the route from O to C through A.

contentBlocks.value: OC is the diagonal from O, and the parallelogram law gives the resultant as the sum of the two sides from O

solutionSteps.instruction: State AC separately for part b.

strategyBlocks.value: Use the parallelogram property to identify AC, then travel from O to C via A.

whyThisWorks.value: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal in length and parallel in direction, and those are precisely the two things a vector records — so opposite sides are literally the same vector, regardless of where they are drawn. That is why AC equals OB, and why the diagonal from the common vertex is the sum of the two sides meeting there: the parallelogram law and the triangle law are the same rule seen from two angles.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing AC = a + b by confusing the side AC with the diagonal OC.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing AC = a + b by confusing the side AC with the diagonal OC.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving AC = −b by reversing the direction; AC runs the same way as OB.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving AC = −b by reversing the direction; AC runs the same way as OB.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the other diagonal BA = a − b when OC was asked for.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using the other diagonal BA = a − b when OC was asked for.

examTip.value: Mark the arrows on a parallelogram diagram before writing anything — equal sides must have arrows pointing the same way to represent the same vector.
